the Mossi were the first to use the horse in the region, and the French were the first to introduce firearms.

The use of firearms in Upper Volta in the late nineteenth century did not lead to the establishment of an empire comparable to the Mossi states; the introduction of firearms did not lead to an increase in military power; firearms were not used in the same way as in the West; the use of firearms was not the result of a conscious policy of modernization; and the use of firearms did not contribute to a change in the social organization of the army.
the military technology of the late nineteenth century in Upper Volta was not as advanced as that of other regions of Africa.
